title: TOKEN SOURCE
rule: one token file paints the page; the hero plate is a real Design System v2 screen that the notes point at
description: A cobalt band with the claim the page proves, 'Every colour on this page comes from one token source.', and under it, 24 px clear of the band, a real Design System v2 screen from its Storybook (buttons and two alerts, invented data) at up to 704 px on a pale plate. Four notes pass under the pinned plate (805 tokens, 36 components, WCAG 2.1 AA, 20 releases); each draws a hairline to the part it names. A note fades as a whole before it reaches the plate. Then three side-column cards in true order (Read to Feed on the live reader, Bayyinah TV, the care platform on its real claims screen), each an 880 × 440 plate and a 280 px column, and a record of ten results.
signature: Gentrit Display (Hubot Sans; its sister face draws the digits) with JetBrains Mono, one cobalt. The page has no palette of its own: the root reads the token file's light values (core, semantic and component tiers), and ground, ink, lines, band, notes and cards all point at those variables, so the claim is literally true; the footnote says the page's colours are its own token file, not Design System v2. Motion: S2, the plate pins while the notes pass; a note that crosses the pin line draws its hairline in 180 ms and rings its part of the screenshot in 120 ms; the previous hairline fades in 120 ms. Hairlines end at parts of the still screen: 805 tokens at the two alerts, 36 components at the two button rows, WCAG 2.1 AA at the information alert, 20 releases at the first solid button. A note fades from 1 to 0 over its last 60 px above the pinned plate's bottom edge (view() timeline, @supports guarded); the pin holds until the note before the last one has gone. S1: three cards oldest first, the covered card scales to 0.96 on a view timeline. Phone: Read to Feed uses its store screenshot and the care card uses the real patients ring. Keyboard: 'Work' jumps to the cards with no travel. Reduced motion: the plate does not pin, notes do not fade, hairlines appear with no draw, no stack scale.

chroma.source: chroma.mjs method (decode and threshold unchanged) on loop5/token-source/final/d-top.png, 1440 × 900

holdback: Lowest: original, 7/10. The frame is still a claim on a colour band, a product plate and a sticky card stack; lifting the plate 24 px off the band removes the launch-page overlap, but the layout a visitor names is the same as round 4. What carries the page is the device: the page is painted by its own hero, the claim says so on the first screen, and the token names on the page change when the source flips. Harmony and hooks are 8.5, not 9: the reader plate is a 512 px scene centred on its own ground, so about 180 px of that ground shows at each side of the 880 px plate, and a visitor must still press Dark to see the hook work. Known limits: during the specimen's 560 ms reveal its view-transition layer paints over the current hairline's inner run and ring (they return at the end of the reveal); the pinned window with the Alert panel lasts 64 px of scroll on desktop and 30 px on the phone before the plate leaves with the last note. Slop 0: the plate no longer overlaps the band.
